title: Activity Event
description: The GitHub public Events API event envelope (data-model.md). Validation rules: id, type, actor, repo, and created_at must be present and correctly typed. An unrecognized-but-well-formed type is not a validation failure - only the three known payload shapes below are checked.

id.description: Unique per event, stable across redelivery - the idempotency key (FR-002).

type.description: The GitHub event type, e.g. PushEvent, IssuesEvent, PullRequestEvent.

actor.description: Only id/login are required - the minimum data-model.md asks for ('id, login, display name'). display_login and the URLs are real GitHub API fields but optional here since nothing in this pipeline depends on them.

repo.description: id/name/url required exactly as data-model.md specifies ('id, name, url') - no optional fields here since the real GitHub API doesn't send any others on this sub-object.

payload.description: No shape required at this level - the three known event types get a conditional shape check below (allOf/if-then); any other type is only required to be an object, so a genuinely unrecognized-but-well-formed type still passes (data-model.md's rule, FR-003/SC-002).

public.description: Deliberately not in the top-level `required` list even though data-model.md's field table lists it - the validation-rules paragraph (what's actually enforced) only requires id/type/actor/repo/created_at.

allOf.description: if/then per known type, not a top-level 'oneOf payload shape', so an event whose type isn't one of these three simply skips payload-shape checking instead of failing to match any branch.
